views.name: product_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  productid,
  NAME,
  productnumber,
  makeflag,
  finishedgoodsflag,
  color,
  safetystocklevel,
  reorderpoint,
  standardcost,
  listprice,
  size,
  sizeunitmeasurecode,
  weightunitmeasurecode,
  weight,
  daystomanufacture,
  productline,
  class,
  style,
  productsubcategoryid,
  productmodelid,
  sellstartdate,
  sellenddate,
  discontinueddate,
  rowguid,
  modifieddate
FROM product

params.description: Row-level product master data (one row per productid) — basic attributes and identifiers for products.
params.when_to_use: Look up product attributes by productid (name, number, flags, dimensions, costs, prices, dates). | Join product descriptive attributes into sales, inventory, or analytics queries as a dimension table. | Compose higher-level aggregations (e.g., count of products, avg listprice) or join to product-category, product-model, or transactional tables while preserving a single row per product.
params.output_schema: productid: Surrogate primary key for the product — derived from product.productid | NAME: Product name/description — derived from product.NAME | productnumber: Business product code/sku — derived from product.productnumber | makeflag: Indicator whether the product is made in-house (boolean/flag) — derived from product.makeflag | finishedgoodsflag: Indicator whether product is a finished good (boolean/flag) — derived from product.finishedgoodsflag | color: Product color attribute — derived from product.color | safetystocklevel: Inventory safety stock threshold (numeric) — derived from product.safetystocklevel | reorderpoint: Inventory reorder point (numeric) — derived from product.reorderpoint | standardcost: Standard cost of the product (numeric/currency) — derived from product.standardcost | listprice: Sales list price of the product (numeric/currency) — derived from product.listprice | size: Size descriptor (text/number) — derived from product.size | sizeunitmeasurecode: Unit of measure code for size — derived from product.sizeunitmeasurecode | weightunitmeasurecode: Unit of measure code for weight — derived from product.weightunitmeasurecode | weight: Product weight (numeric) — derived from product.weight | daystomanufacture: Manufacturing lead time in days (integer) — derived from product.daystomanufacture | productline: High-level product line/category code (text) — derived from product.productline | class: Product class (text) — derived from product.class | style: Product style (text) — derived from product.style | productsubcategoryid: FK to product subcategory (nullable) — derived from product.productsubcategoryid | productmodelid: FK to product model (nullable) — derived from product.productmodelid | sellstartdate: Date when the product becomes available for sale — derived from product.sellstartdate | sellenddate: Date when the product is no longer sold (nullable) — derived from product.sellenddate | discontinueddate: Date the product was discontinued (nullable) — derived from product.discontinueddate | rowguid: Row GUID for replication/identification — derived from product.rowguid | modifieddate: Last modified timestamp for the product row — derived from product.modifieddate
params.grounded_columns: product.productid | product.NAME | product.productnumber | product.makeflag | product.finishedgoodsflag | product.color | product.safetystocklevel | product.reorderpoint | product.standardcost | product.listprice | product.size | product.sizeunitmeasurecode | product.weightunitmeasurecode | product.weight | product.daystomanufacture | product.productline | product.class | product.style | product.productsubcategoryid | product.productmodelid | product.sellstartdate | product.sellenddate | product.discontinueddate | product.rowguid | product.modifieddate
params.metric: This view exposes no derived aggregates; all outputs are direct column projections from the base table. | Examples of metrics you can compute by aggregating this view: | product_count = COUNT(productid) | avg_listprice = AVG(listprice) | avg_standardcost = AVG(standardcost) | count_by_productline = COUNT(productid) GROUP BY productline
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_with_category on productid — safe because both views are 1 row per productid (product_with_category is a JOIN that preserves productid uniqueness), so joining will not duplicate product-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_review_stats (aggregated by productid) on productid — safe because product_review_stats is pre-aggregated per productid; it will not multiply rows when joined to this one-row-per-product view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to productmodel or productsubcategory dimension tables on productmodelid or productsubcategoryid respectively — safe if those dimensions are one-row-per-id, because this view is one-row-per-productid and dimensions are 1:1 to their id. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to sales_orders_flat, sales_by_order (if they are one-to-many at product-level) or any transaction-level table that contains multiple sales rows per productid, because those are one-to-many relative to this view and will multiply product rows and any derived measures (e.g., costs/prices) unless you aggregate the transactional side first (e.g., SUM(qty) GROUP BY productid) or restrict to a single row via aggregation/windowing. | do NOT join directly to sibling JOIN views that expand product into orders (e.g., sales_orders_flat) unless you intend to produce a transaction-grain result; to preserve product-level cardinality, first aggregate the transactional view to productid. | When composing metrics: if you need metrics like total_sales_amount per product, compute total_sales_amount = SUM(sales_amount) from the transactional source grouped by productid, then JOIN that aggregated result to product_basic ON productid — this preserves correct cardinality and prevents double-counting. | If joining to any RANK or HISTORY view (e.g., salesorderheader_rank_by_date, currencyrate_latest_per_pair), ensure the target view is at most one row per join key (productid or other key). If the rank/history view is multi-row per key, reduce it to one row per key before joining.

views.description: Normalized product dimension: one row per product with key descriptive attributes and core measures (listprice, standardcost). Useful as a clean product lookup for joins or downstream aggregations. | Use for: List product attributes for reporting or join to sales/order lines; Filter products by category/subcategory/model or price ranges; Compute product-level margins using listprice and standardcost

views.name: product_with_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.productid,
  p.NAME,
  p.productnumber,
  p.productsubcategoryid,
  p.productmodelid,
  p.listprice,
  p.standardcost,
  p.productline,
  p.class,
  p.style,
  p.rowguid,
  p.modifieddate,
  ps.productsubcategoryid AS productsubcategory_productsubcategoryid,
  ps.productcategoryid AS productsubcategory_productcategoryid,
  ps.name AS productsubcategory_name,
  pc.productcategoryid AS productcategory_productcategoryid,
  pc.name AS productcategory_name
FROM product p
LEFT JOIN productsubcategory ps ON p.productsubcategoryid = ps.productsubcategoryid
LEFT JOIN productcategory pc ON ps.productcategoryid = pc.productcategoryid

params.description: A denormalized product-level view enriched with its subcategory and category attributes; answers product detail and product-to-category lookup questions.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve product details (price, cost, identifiers) for a single product or set of products by productid, name, productnumber, or productsubcategory/productcategory. | Filter and list products by category or subcategory attributes (category name, subcategory name, productline, class, style). | Serve as a stable product dimension when composing with sales/order facts or other aggregations (use this view as the product-side of joins). | Build higher-level aggregates by grouping on product attributes (e.g., listprice distributions by category) — ensure aggregation is applied after joining any many-side facts.
params.output_schema: productid: Product identifier from product.productid (grain: one row per productid). | NAME: Product name from product.NAME. | productnumber: Product number/code from product.productnumber. | productsubcategoryid: Foreign key on product pointing to productsubcategory.productsubcategoryid (may be NULL). | productmodelid: Foreign key from product.productmodelid (product model id). | listprice: Product list price from product.listprice (numeric/monetary attribute). | standardcost: Product standard cost from product.standardcost (numeric/monetary attribute). | productline: Product line attribute from product.productline (categorical). | class: Product class attribute from product.class (categorical). | style: Product style attribute from product.style (categorical). | rowguid: rowguid from product.rowguid (unique identifier). | modifieddate: Last modified datetime from product.modifieddate. | productsubcategory_productsubcategoryid: productsubcategory.productsubcategoryid (renamed to show provenance) — equals product.productsubcategoryid when not NULL. | productsubcategory_productcategoryid: productsubcategory.productcategoryid (FK from subcategory to category, may be NULL). | productsubcategory_name: productsubcategory.name (subcategory name, may be NULL). | productcategory_productcategoryid: productcategory.productcategoryid (category id, may be NULL). | productcategory_name: productcategory.name (category name, may be NULL).
params.grounded_columns: product.productid | product.NAME | product.productnumber | product.productsubcategoryid | product.productmodelid | product.listprice | product.standardcost | product.productline | product.class | product.style | product.rowguid | product.modifieddate | productsubcategory.productsubcategoryid | productsubcategory.productcategoryid | productsubcategory.name | productcategory.productcategoryid | productcategory.name
params.metric: listprice = direct attribute (no aggregation) derived from product.listprice | standardcost = direct attribute (no aggregation) derived from product.standardcost
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables that reference product.productid (for example sales/order fact views) on productid — safe because this view has one row per productid (product is the one-side) so joining facts will not duplicate product rows but instead expand rows per fact. | Safe to join to normalized product dimension views (e.g., product_basic) on productid — both are one-row-per-productid so measures from this view (none are aggregates) are not duplicated. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child without aggregation on the many side (for example: product -> reviews or product -> order lines) unless you intend row multiplication. If you need aggregated measures from a many-side (e.g., total sales, review counts), pre-aggregate the many-side (SUM/COUNT by productid) or use an aggregate sibling view (e.g., sales_by_order, product_review_stats) that is already grouped by productid before joining. | When joining via the subcategory/category keys: joining additional tables on productsubcategory.productsubcategoryid or productcategory.productcategoryid is safe only if those tables are one-row-per-(sub)category. Joining a one-to-many table keyed to productcategory/productsubcategory (for example category->sub-sub-entities) without pre-aggregation will multiply products that share the same category; aggregate first by productid or by the category key as appropriate. | When composing further aggregates: treat listprice and standardcost as base numeric attributes. If you aggregate across products (e.g., AVG(listprice) by category), compute aggregates after grouping; do not rely on row-count-sensitive expressions without explicit aggregation. | Null propagation: productsubcategory and productcategory columns may be NULL for products without a subcategory; joins on productsubcategoryid are LEFT JOINs in the source SQL, so downstream inner joins on these derived subcategory/category columns will filter out products that lack those relationships — use LEFT JOIN if you want to preserve all products.

views.description: Denormalized product rows joined to subcategory and category names. One row per product with productcategory and productsubcategory context for reporting and aggregation by category. | Use for: Aggregate sales by product category/subcategory; List products with category context; Filter products belonging to categories or subcategories

views.name: sales_orders_flat
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sod.salesorderid,
  sod.salesorderdetailid,
  sod.orderqty,
  sod.productid,
  sod.specialofferid,
  sod.unitprice,
  sod.unitpricediscount,
  sod.rowguid AS rowguid,
  sod.modifieddate AS modifieddate,
  soh.orderdate,
  soh.duedate,
  soh.shipdate,
  soh.STATUS,
  soh.onlineorderflag,
  soh.customerid,
  soh.salespersonid,
  soh.territoryid,
  soh.subtotal,
  soh.taxamt,
  soh.freight,
  soh.totaldue,
  p.NAME AS NAME,
  p.listprice AS listprice,
  (sod.unitprice * sod.orderqty * (1.0 - COALESCE(sod.unitpricediscount,0.0))) AS line_extended_amount
FROM salesorderdetail sod
LEFT JOIN salesorderheader soh ON sod.salesorderid = soh.salesorderid
LEFT JOIN product p ON sod.productid = p.productid

params.description: Flattened sales order lines with their header and product attributes — answers questions about individual order line rows, line amounts, and joins of line-level data to header- and product-level attributes.
params.when_to_use: Report or analysis at the sales order line grain (each salesorderdetail) such as line-level revenue, quantities, discounts, dates, and related header/product attributes. | Compose aggregations by grouping these rows (e.g., total sales, average discount, units sold) because the view is at the line-item grain. | Filter or slice order-lines by order header attributes (orderdate, status, customer, territory) or product attributes (name, listprice). | Use as the base for time series, cohort, or customer/product-level aggregations by re-aggregating this view (do NOT join 1-to-many dimensions without re-aggregation).
params.output_schema: salesorderid: sales order identifier, from salesorderdetail.salesorderid (joined to salesorderheader.salesorderid in this view) | salesorderdetailid: sales order line identifier (the view grain), from salesorderdetail.salesorderdetailid | orderqty: quantity ordered on the line, from salesorderdetail.orderqty | productid: product identifier for the line, from salesorderdetail.productid | specialofferid: special offer applied to the line, from salesorderdetail.specialofferid | unitprice: unit price recorded on the sales line, from salesorderdetail.unitprice | unitpricediscount: discount rate on the unit price (nullable), from salesorderdetail.unitpricediscount | rowguid: row GUID for the salesorderdetail row, from salesorderdetail.rowguid | modifieddate: last modified date for the salesorderdetail row, from salesorderdetail.modifieddate | orderdate: order header order date, from salesorderheader.orderdate (via LEFT JOIN on salesorderid) | duedate: order header due date, from salesorderheader.duedate | shipdate: order header ship date, from salesorderheader.shipdate | STATUS: order header status, from salesorderheader.STATUS | onlineorderflag: header flag whether order was placed online, from salesorderheader.onlineorderflag | customerid: header customer id, from salesorderheader.customerid | salespersonid: header salesperson id, from salesorderheader.salespersonid | territoryid: header territory id, from salesorderheader.territoryid | subtotal: header-level subtotal for the order, from salesorderheader.subtotal | taxamt: header-level tax amount, from salesorderheader.taxamt | freight: header-level freight charge, from salesorderheader.freight | totaldue: header-level total due, from salesorderheader.totaldue | NAME: product name for the line's product, from product.NAME (joined on productid) | listprice: product list price, from product.listprice | line_extended_amount: computed line amount after quantity and discount = (unitprice * orderqty * (1.0 - COALESCE(unitpricediscount, 0.0))) derived from salesorderdetail.unitprice, salesorderdetail.orderqty, salesorderdetail.unitpricediscount
params.grounded_columns: salesorderdetail.salesorderid | salesorderdetail.salesorderdetailid | salesorderdetail.orderqty | salesorderdetail.productid | salesorderdetail.specialofferid | salesorderdetail.unitprice | salesorderdetail.unitpricediscount | salesorderdetail.rowguid | salesorderdetail.modifieddate | salesorderheader.orderdate | salesorderheader.duedate | salesorderheader.shipdate | salesorderheader.STATUS | salesorderheader.onlineorderflag | salesorderheader.customerid | salesorderheader.salespersonid | salesorderheader.territoryid | salesorderheader.subtotal | salesorderheader.taxamt | salesorderheader.freight | salesorderheader.totaldue | product.NAME | product.listprice
params.metric: line_extended_amount = unitprice * orderqty * (1.0 - COALESCE(unitpricediscount, 0.0))  -- line-level extended revenue (non-aggregated). | Note: subtotal, taxamt, freight, totaldue are header-level measures included via the LEFT JOIN; they are not per-line aggregates and represent the order header's totals.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_basic or product_with_category on productid — safe because product is a 1-to-1 (or many-to-one from lines to product) dimension keyed by productid; joining will not duplicate line measures (each line has at most one product row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salesorderheader (or salesorderheader-based views like salesorderheader_rank_by_date) on salesorderid — safe because salesorderheader is 1-to-1 per salesorderid and this view already LEFT JOINs header; joining additional header-level attributes keyed by salesorderid will not multiply measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many analytical aggregates or raw transaction tables (for example, do NOT join to product_review_stats or sales_by_order without keys/aggregation) unless you aggregate the many-side to the same grain first. Joining an un-aggregated one-to-many table on productid or salesorderid will multiply this view's line rows and overcount measures like line_extended_amount. | When joining to sibling AGG views (sales_by_order, salesperson_performance_agg, product_review_stats, territory_sales_trend): ensure those aggregates are at a cardinality that is <= the join key (e.g., sales_by_order aggregated to salesorderid is safe to join on salesorderid because it's 1 row per order). Do NOT join to an AGG that is at a lower grain (multiple rows per productid or orderid) without re-aggregating to one row per join key. | If you need to attach multi-row detail (e.g., multiple reviews per product), either: a) pre-aggregate that detail to one row per productid (e.g., avg_rating) before joining, or b) join and then re-aggregate starting from this view's grain to avoid duplication. | Because this view's grain is ['salesorderid','salesorderdetailid'], any join that is many-to-one from this grain (i.e., dimensions keyed by productid or salesorderid) is safe; any join that is one-to-many relative to this grain (additional line-level details or multiple reviews per line) is unsafe without aggregation.

views.description: Denormalized sales order lines joined to order header and product to produce one row per sales order line with order-level and product-level attributes and line revenue measures. | Use for: Compute revenue or quantity by product, salesperson, territory, date ranges; Identify high-value order lines or returns (joins to product attributes); Feed into time-series aggregation by orderdate

views.name: sales_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  soh.salesorderid,
  soh.orderdate,
  soh.customerid,
  soh.salespersonid,
  soh.territoryid,
  COUNT(sod.salesorderdetailid) AS order_line_count,
  SUM(sod.orderqty) AS total_order_qty,
  SUM(sod.unitprice * sod.orderqty * (1.0 - COALESCE(sod.unitpricediscount,0.0))) AS total_order_amount,
  soh.subtotal,
  soh.taxamt,
  soh.freight,
  soh.totaldue
FROM salesorderheader soh
LEFT JOIN salesorderdetail sod ON soh.salesorderid = sod.salesorderid
GROUP BY soh.salesorderid, soh.orderdate, soh.customerid, soh.salespersonid, soh.territoryid, soh.subtotal, soh.taxamt, soh.freight, soh.totaldue

params.description: Aggregated sales order-level measures and identifiers: one row per salesorderid with order header fields and order-line derived metrics.
params.when_to_use: Report or query needing order-level totals (line count, total quantity, amount) alongside header amounts (subtotal, tax, freight, totaldue). | Drill-to-order workflows that start from orders and need summed line-item metrics. | Composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., customer or salesperson totals) by re-aggregating this view. | Joining order-level attributes to dimensions (customer, salesperson, territory, date) without duplicating measures.
params.output_schema: salesorderid: Surrogate/PK for the sales order — derived from salesorderheader.salesorderid | orderdate: Order date/time from the order header — derived from salesorderheader.orderdate | customerid: FK to customer for this order — derived from salesorderheader.customerid | salespersonid: FK to salesperson for this order — derived from salesorderheader.salespersonid | territoryid: FK to sales territory for this order — derived from salesorderheader.territoryid | order_line_count: Count of detail lines on the order — derived metric COUNT(salesorderdetail.salesorderdetailid) | total_order_qty: Sum of order quantities across lines — derived metric SUM(salesorderdetail.orderqty) | total_order_amount: Sum of line extended amounts after discount — derived metric SUM(unitprice * orderqty * (1 - COALESCE(unitpricediscount,0.0))) from salesorderdetail | subtotal: Header subtotal amount (already on header) — derived from salesorderheader.subtotal | taxamt: Header tax amount — derived from salesorderheader.taxamt | freight: Header freight amount — derived from salesorderheader.freight | totaldue: Header total due amount — derived from salesorderheader.totaldue
params.grounded_columns: salesorderheader.salesorderid | salesorderheader.orderdate | salesorderheader.customerid | salesorderheader.salespersonid | salesorderheader.territoryid | salesorderheader.subtotal | salesorderheader.taxamt | salesorderheader.freight | salesorderheader.totaldue | salesorderdetail.salesorderdetailid | salesorderdetail.salesorderid | salesorderdetail.orderqty | salesorderdetail.unitprice | salesorderdetail.unitpricediscount
params.metric: order_line_count = COUNT(salesorderdetail.salesorderdetailid)  -- one row per order: number of detail rows | total_order_qty = SUM(salesorderdetail.orderqty)  -- total units ordered across lines on the order | total_order_amount = SUM(salesorderdetail.unitprice * salesorderdetail.orderqty * (1.0 - COALESCE(salesorderdetail.unitpricediscount,0.0)))  -- sum of extended line amounts after discounts | subtotal = salesorderheader.subtotal  -- header-stored subtotal (not recomputed from line items in this view) | taxamt = salesorderheader.taxamt  -- header-stored tax amount | freight = salesorderheader.freight  -- header-stored freight | totaldue = salesorderheader.totaldue  -- header-stored total due
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer dimension/table on sales_by_order.customerid = customer.customerid — safe because sales_by_order is one-row-per-salesorderid; joining to the (dimension) customer (1 row per customer) does not duplicate order measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salesperson dimension/table on sales_by_order.salespersonid = salesperson.salespersonid — safe for the same reason (dimensions are 1-to-1 per id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to territory dimension/table on sales_by_order.territoryid = territory.territoryid — safe when territory is a 1-row-per-territory dimension. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date/day dimension on sales_by_order.orderdate = date_dim.datekey (or appropriate key) — safe because date dimension is 1-to-1 per date value. | re-aggregation guidance: to produce customer- or salesperson-level totals, aggregate (SUM) the measures from this view grouped by customerid or salespersonid (e.g., SUM(total_order_amount) grouped by customerid). Do not rely on joining this view to line-level tables before aggregating, as that may double-count. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many child table (for example, a detailed payments table, order-attachments, or product reviews) without first ensuring uniqueness on the child side or re-aggregating, because such joins can multiply rows and therefore duplicate the aggregated measures (order_line_count, total_order_qty, total_order_amount). | do NOT join this view to salesorderdetail (or any other order-detail table) on salesorderid unless you either: a) aggregate the joined detail rows back to order-level (GROUP BY salesorderid) before selecting measures, or b) join to a deduplicated/detail-aggregated subquery, because salesorderdetail is many-per-order and will multiply order-level metrics. | compatibility with sibling views: you may join to product_basic, product_with_category, product_review_stats only through an order->line->product path if you first aggregate or restrict to one row per order (e.g., pre-aggregate product-related metrics per order) — otherwise the many-to-many expansion between this order-level view and product-level tables will duplicate measures. | composition note for higher-level aggregations: this view is already aggregated to salesorderid grain. Any composition that needs a coarser grain (customer, salesperson, territory, date) should SUM the measure columns from this view and GROUP BY the target key to remain cardinality-safe.

views.description: Aggregate measures at the salesorderid (order) level: total_order_qty and total_order_amount derived from order lines, joined to order header. Useful for order-level KPIs and trend analysis. | Use for: Order-level revenue and quantity reporting; Comparing aggregated line totals to header totals for data quality; Filtering orders by salesperson/territory and aggregating metrics

views.name: salesperson_quota_history_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  BusinessEntityID,
  QuotaDate,
  SalesQuota,
  rowguid,
  ModifiedDate
FROM SalesPersonQuotaHistory

params.description: One-row-per-person-per-quota-date history of sales quotas assigned to salespeople; answers questions about salesperson quota amounts and their effective dates.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the SalesQuota value for a given salesperson and quota date | Trend or time-series of quotas for a salesperson (after joining to a date dimension or ordering by QuotaDate) | Filter or slice sales metrics by the quota effective date (e.g., compare actual sales to quota on matching dates) when used as a normalized lookup | As a stable grain source when composing aggregates by BusinessEntityID and QuotaDate (use this view as the dimensional/measure source for quotas)
params.output_schema: BusinessEntityID: identifier of the salesperson (from SalesPersonQuotaHistory.BusinessEntityID) | QuotaDate: date the quota applies to (from SalesPersonQuotaHistory.QuotaDate) | SalesQuota: monetary quota amount assigned for that BusinessEntityID on QuotaDate (from SalesPersonQuotaHistory.SalesQuota) | rowguid: row-level GUID for the source record (from SalesPersonQuotaHistory.rowguid) | ModifiedDate: last-modified timestamp of the quota record (from SalesPersonQuotaHistory.ModifiedDate)
params.metric: SalesQuota = SalesPersonQuotaHistory.SalesQuota (atomic stored monetary value; NOT an aggregate in this view) | No aggregated metrics are produced by this view; every output is a direct projection of base columns
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salesperson dimension or person table on BusinessEntityID — safe because this view is one-row-per-(BusinessEntityID, QuotaDate) so joining to a 1:1 salesperson dimension will not duplicate SalesQuota. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date/dimension table on QuotaDate — safe because date dimension is 1:1 per date and will not duplicate rows. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many transactional/line-level sales tables (for example sales_orders_flat, sales_by_order, or other order-line level views) without first aggregating those tables to BusinessEntityID and QuotaDate (or BusinessEntityID and a compatible date grain). Joining this view to a raw orders or line-items table will multiply quota rows across many order rows and incorrectly inflate per-row interpretations of SalesQuota. | when combining SalesQuota with aggregated sales measures (e.g., total sales per BusinessEntityID per date), aggregate the sales side to the same grain (BusinessEntityID, QuotaDate) before joining, or join first and then re-aggregate with appropriate grouping to avoid duplicating SalesQuota. | do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are at a finer grain than (BusinessEntityID, QuotaDate) unless those AGG views are first reduced to this view's grain: e.g., sales_by_order (AGG) or salesperson_performance_agg (AGG) may be aggregated at different date keys — confirm their grain then align/aggregate by BusinessEntityID+QuotaDate to preserve measure correctness. | safe composition example: JOIN salesperson_quota_history_norm NORM ON NORM.BusinessEntityID = salesperson_dim.BusinessEntityID — safe because salesperson_dim is one row per BusinessEntityID. | unsafe composition example: JOIN sales_orders_flat ON sales_orders_flat.SalesPersonID = NORM.BusinessEntityID — unsafe unless sales_orders_flat is pre-aggregated to (BusinessEntityID, QuotaDate) because multiple orders per quota date would duplicate SalesQuota values.

views.description: Normalized SalesPerson quota history with consistent column names and parsed date. One row per quota history record to analyze quotas over time per BusinessEntityID. | Use for: Trend analysis of salesperson quotas over time; Join quotas to salesperson current state to compute attainment vs quota

views.name: salesperson_performance_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  soh.salespersonid,
  COUNT(DISTINCT soh.salesorderid) AS orders_count,
  SUM(soh.subtotal) AS sum_subtotal,
  SUM(soh.totaldue) AS sum_totaldue,
  AVG(soh.totaldue) AS avg_order_totaldue
FROM salesorderheader soh
GROUP BY soh.salespersonid

params.description: Summarizes order-level measures per salesperson: count of orders, sums of subtotal and totaldue, and average order totaldue, grouped by salespersonid.
params.when_to_use: Report total orders and revenue-related metrics per salesperson for a given time window when salesorderheader rows are already filtered upstream. | Compose into dashboards or SQL that compare salesperson performance (orders_count, sum_subtotal, sum_totaldue, avg_order_totaldue). | Join with salesperson/dimension views that are one-row-per-salesperson to add attributes (name, region, quota) without re-aggregation. | As a building block for higher-level rollups (e.g., territory or region) by summing its measures across multiple salespersons.
params.output_schema: salespersonid: identifier of the salesperson; sourced from salesorderheader.salespersonid (GROUP BY key). | orders_count: number of distinct sales orders for that salesperson; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT salesorderheader.salesorderid). | sum_subtotal: sum of salesorderheader.subtotal across orders for that salesperson; derived from SUM(salesorderheader.subtotal). | sum_totaldue: sum of salesorderheader.totaldue across orders for that salesperson; derived from SUM(salesorderheader.totaldue). | avg_order_totaldue: average order totaldue for that salesperson; derived from AVG(salesorderheader.totaldue).
params.metric: orders_count = COUNT(DISTINCT salesorderheader.salesorderid) | sum_subtotal = SUM(salesorderheader.subtotal) | sum_totaldue = SUM(salesorderheader.totaldue) | avg_order_totaldue = AVG(salesorderheader.totaldue)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any salesperson/dimension (one-row-per-salesperson) such as a normalized salesperson table or view on salespersonid — safe because this view is one-row-per-salesperson so measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: aggregate-then-join to territory-level views by grouping/adding this view's numeric measures across salespersonid when building territory summaries (safe because you are summing one-row-per-salesperson rows). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables or views (for example, orders, order line items, product reviews, or any sibling JOIN views that expand orders into multiple rows) without re-aggregating first — such joins will multiply rows and overcount orders_count and sum_* measures. | do NOT join to salesorderheader (or any view that contains the raw orders repeated) on salespersonid and then select measures from this view without re-aggregation, because joining back to the source order rows will duplicate the aggregated measures. | If you need to enrich by a many-to-one relationship (many salespersons per territory) join on the key from the one side to this view (e.g., territory -> salesperson via salespersonid) only when the join preserves one-row-per-salesperson; otherwise, first aggregate the many-side to salespersonid before joining. | When composing into further aggregations (e.g., compute average salesperson revenue per territory), treat sum_subtotal and sum_totaldue as additive metrics (can be SUM()'d across salespersons), treat orders_count as an additive distinct-order count only if underlying orders are disjoint across salespersons (they are, since salesorderheader.salespersonid is the grouping key), and compute weighted averages from sum_totaldue / orders_count or use avg_order_totaldue only as a per-salesperson-level average (do not average avg_order_totaldue across salespersons without weighting).

views.description: Aggregated sales metrics per salesperson across order headers: count of orders, total_subtotal and total_totaldue. One row per salesperson. Useful for ranking salespeople by revenue or activity. | Use for: Rank or compare salesperson revenue and activity; Join to salesperson table to compute attainment vs quota or commissions

views.name: product_review_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  productid,
  COUNT(productreviewid) AS review_count,
  AVG(rating) AS avg_rating,
  MAX(reviewdate) AS most_recent_review_date
FROM productreview
GROUP BY productid

params.description: Aggregated per-product review statistics: count of reviews, average rating, and most recent review date for each product.
params.when_to_use: Get review-level summary metrics for a specific product or set of products (e.g., review_count, avg_rating). | Join product review summaries to product master data (name, category, etc.) without changing aggregated counts. | Filter or slice product-level review metrics by product attributes (category, brand) or by time windows using the most_recent_review_date. | Compose into higher-level aggregates (e.g., category-level average rating) by re-aggregating the per-product metrics.
params.output_schema: productid: identifier of the product — derived from productreview.productid (group key). | review_count: number of reviews for the product — derived from COUNT(productreview.productreviewid) in productreview. | avg_rating: average rating across all reviews for the product — derived from AVG(productreview.rating) in productreview. | most_recent_review_date: the latest review date for the product — derived from MAX(productreview.reviewdate) in productreview.
params.metric: review_count = COUNT(productreview.productreviewid) | avg_rating = AVG(productreview.rating) | most_recent_review_date = MAX(productreview.reviewdate)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_basic (NORM) on productid — safe because product_basic is one-row-per-product, so joining will not duplicate review_count or avg_rating. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_with_category (JOIN) on productid — safe when product_with_category is one-row-per-product (product attributes); this does not duplicate measures and is appropriate to add product attributes like category for slicing. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salesperson_quota_history_norm (NORM) — do NOT join directly on productid (not a relevant key); only join on keys that are one-to-one with productid if such exist, otherwise it will multiply rows. | do NOT join without care to any one-to-many-detail table or view (for example, joining to sales_orders_flat or sales_by_order) on productid without re-aggregation — these are many-orders-per-product and will duplicate review_count and avg_rating. If you need combined analysis, either: | - re-aggregate the joined result after the join (e.g., GROUP BY productid and SUM or AVG appropriately), or | - pre-aggregate the other side to one-row-per-product (e.g., aggregate sales_by_order to product-level sales_by_product) then join on productid. | When composing to compute category-level metrics: join product_review_stats to product_with_category on productid (one-row-per-product) and then aggregate over category (e.g., SUM(review_count) or AVG(avg_rating) weighted appropriately). | When combining with time-based trend views (e.g., salesorderheader_rank_by_date or territory_sales_trend): avoid joining directly on productid if those views are multi-row per product per time period; instead, align on productid and time after appropriate aggregation (for example, extract most_recent_review_date and compare to sales time windows). | Rationale: product_review_stats is one-row-per-product (grain = productid). Joins that are one-to-one or many-to-one into this view (dimensions with single row per product) will not duplicate its measures. Joins that are one-to-many (orders, sales lines, multiple rankings or time series per product) will multiply rows and thereby multiply review_count/avg_rating unless the query re-aggregates these measures after the join.

views.description: Aggregated review metrics per product: count of reviews, average rating, and most recent review date. One row per product. Useful for product quality signals and filtering by popularity or rating. | Use for: Find products with highest average rating or most reviews; Join review aggregates to product listings or sales to study impact of reviews on sales

views.name: salesorderheader_rank_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  salesorderid,
  customerid,
  orderdate,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customerid ORDER BY orderdate DESC, salesorderid DESC) AS order_rank
FROM salesorderheader

params.description: Ranks each sales order per customer by order date (most recent = 1), returning one row per salesorderid with its per-customer rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the N most recent or oldest orders per customer (e.g., latest order, second-latest). | Filter orders to a particular per-customer rank (e.g., only rank = 1 for latest orders) before joining to other tables. | Compose into analytics that need an order-level row plus its position in the customer's order history (e.g., retention, repeat-purchase sequencing). | Use as an input to aggregations that operate at customer granularity after selecting a rank subset (e.g., count customers whose latest order is within a date range).
params.output_schema: salesorderid: unique identifier of the sales order — derived from base column salesorderheader.salesorderid | customerid: identifier of the customer who placed the order — derived from base column salesorderheader.customerid | orderdate: date (and time) when the order was placed — derived from base column salesorderheader.orderdate | order_rank: integer row-number ranking of orders per customer, ordered by orderdate DESC, salesorderid DESC — defined by ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customerid ORDER BY orderdate DESC, salesorderid DESC)
params.metric: order_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY salesorderheader.customerid ORDER BY salesorderheader.orderdate DESC, salesorderheader.salesorderid DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer dimension (or a view that is one-row-per-customer) on salesorderheader.customerid = customer.customerid — safe because this view is one-row-per-salesorderid and joining to a one-row-per-customer dimension will not duplicate order rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_basic or product_with_category only via a pre-aggregated order-line level view keyed by salesorderid (NOT directly) — the current view has one row per order but product views are product-level; joining directly on product keys is not applicable and would not enrich this view without order-line linkage. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sales_by_order (an aggregate at salesorderid) on salesorderid — safe because sales_by_order is one-row-per-salesorderid, so measures will not be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views that expand orders into lines or reviews (for example: order_lines, product_review_stats which is per-product or per-product-review granularity) without re-aggregating back to salesorderid first, because those joins would multiply this view's rows and incorrectly duplicate measures derived per order. | do NOT join to multi-row-per-order aggregates (or detailed transaction tables) without either (a) joining on a 1:1 key (e.g., salesorderid when the other side is aggregated to salesorderid) or (b) re-aggregating the result after the join, because order_rank is defined per salesorderid and will otherwise be repeated across joined child rows. | When composing into customer-level metrics: if you aggregate this view up to customerid (for example, COUNT(*) FILTER (order_rank = 1) to count latest orders), that aggregation is safe and expected. Avoid joining this view to a customer-level aggregate and then aggregating again unless you handle duplicates — prefer joining to one-row-per-customer sources. | Example safe composition patterns: (a) filter where order_rank = 1 and join to customer or territory views to compute metrics about customers' latest orders; (b) join to sales_by_order (salesorderid) to attach order totals then aggregate by customer without duplication. | Example unsafe pattern: joining this view to product_review_stats or any order-line detail directly, because those are many rows per order and will multiply order_rank occurrences — instead, aggregate the detail up to salesorderid first (e.g., SUM(qty) GROUP BY salesorderid) then join.

views.description: Ranked orders per customer by orderdate (1 = most recent). One row per salesorderid with customer-level order rank. Useful for selecting latest-N orders per customer. | Use for: Get latest order(s) per customer; Analyze customer recency or compute metrics on recent orders

views.name: territory_sales_trend
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  soh.territoryid,
  DATE(soh.orderdate) AS order_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT soh.salesorderid) AS orders_count,
  SUM(soh.subtotal) AS sum_subtotal,
  SUM(soh.totaldue) AS sum_totaldue
FROM salesorderheader soh
GROUP BY soh.territoryid, DATE(soh.orderdate)

params.description: Daily per-territory sales rollup: counts of unique orders and daily sums of subtotal and totaldue by territory and order date.
params.when_to_use: Report daily sales performance for each sales territory (e.g., daily orders, subtotal and totaldue by territory). | Compose higher-level time aggregations (weekly/monthly) of territory sales by re-aggregating the view's outputs by date buckets. | Join territory-level daily sales to territory or salesperson dimension attributes to produce enriched reports without recomputing base aggregates. | Build trend analyses, moving averages, or time-series forecasts at the territory × day grain by using the view as the base series.
params.output_schema: territoryid: territory identifier — derived from salesorderheader.territoryid | order_date: order date (date only) — derived from DATE(salesorderheader.orderdate) | orders_count: distinct count of sales orders for the territory on that date — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT salesorderheader.salesorderid) | sum_subtotal: sum of salesorderheader.subtotal for the territory on that date — derived from SUM(salesorderheader.subtotal) | sum_totaldue: sum of salesorderheader.totaldue for the territory on that date — derived from SUM(salesorderheader.totaldue)
params.metric: orders_count = COUNT(DISTINCT salesorderheader.salesorderid)  -- unique sales orders per territory × order_date | sum_subtotal = SUM(salesorderheader.subtotal)  -- additive monetary metric per territory × order_date | sum_totaldue = SUM(salesorderheader.totaldue)  -- additive monetary metric per territory × order_date
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a territory dimension (e.g., territory table/view keyed by territoryid) on territoryid — safe because territory_sales_trend is one-row-per (territoryid, order_date) so joining to a single-row-per-territory dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date/calendar dimension keyed by order_date (or to a normalized orders-by-day view keyed by date) — safe because calendar/date dimension is one-row-per-date. | do NOT join directly to salesorderheader or any other one-to-many detail table (e.g., order line items) without first aggregating that detail to the same grain (territoryid, order_date) — doing so would multiply rows and over-count the measures in this view. | do NOT join to one-to-many views (for example, order-lines, product_review_stats if it is per-order-line or per-product-review) on territoryid or order_date without re-aggregation or using DISTINCT-preserving strategies, because those joins would duplicate the territory_sales_trend aggregated measures. | safe composition pattern for enrichment: LEFT JOIN territory_sales_trend to a territory dimension on territoryid and to a date dimension on order_date, then optionally SUM(orders_count)/SUM(sum_subtotal)/SUM(sum_totaldue) over the joined rows to roll up to coarser time or territory hierarchies — re-aggregation preserves correctness because the view's metrics are additive at its grain. | when joining to other aggregated views, ensure the other view's grain aligns or is a superset/subset that can be safely aggregated/rolled up to (territoryid, order_date). If the other view has a finer grain, aggregate it to (territoryid, order_date) first; if it has a coarser grain, join on the matching keys and avoid duplicating rows by aggregating this view up to that coarser grain before joining.

views.description: Aggregated sales totals by territory and orderdate (date grain): daily/weekly/monthly rollups can be derived by grouping on orderdate. One row per territory x orderdate. | Use for: Time series of sales by territory; Compare territory performance across time windows

views.name: currencyrate_latest_per_pair
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  currencyrateid,
  currencyratedate,
  fromcurrencycode,
  tocurrencycode,
  averagerate,
  endofdayrate,
  modifieddate,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fromcurrencycode, tocurrencycode ORDER BY currencyratedate DESC, currencyrateid DESC) AS pair_rate_rank
FROM currencyrate

params.description: Latest-ranked currency rate rows per currency pair (fromcurrencycode, tocurrencycode) with a row-number rank ordering by date and id.
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent exchange rate row(s) per currency pair (e.g., latest per from/to currency). | Compose queries that need the latest end-of-day or average rate per currency pair by selecting rows where pair_rate_rank = 1. | Filter or join only the top-ranked/latest currencyrate rows into larger analyses (for example, apply latest rates to convert monetary metrics). | Build time-insensitive currency-pair lookups where you want the most recent canonical rate row rather than aggregating across many rate dates.
params.output_schema: currencyrateid: unique identifier for the currencyrate row — derives directly from currencyrate.currencyrateid | currencyratedate: date/time when the rate was effective — derives directly from currencyrate.currencyratedate | fromcurrencycode: source currency code for the rate pair — derives directly from currencyrate.fromcurrencycode | tocurrencycode: target currency code for the rate pair — derives directly from currencyrate.tocurrencycode | averagerate: average exchange rate value recorded for that row — derives directly from currencyrate.averagerate | endofdayrate: end-of-day exchange rate value recorded for that row — derives directly from currencyrate.endofdayrate | modifieddate: last-modified timestamp for the row — derives directly from currencyrate.modifieddate | pair_rate_rank: integer row number ranking within (fromcurrencycode, tocurrencycode) partition ordered by currencyratedate DESC, currencyrateid DESC — derived via ROW_NUMBER() window over currencyrate
params.grounded_columns: currencyrate.currencyrateid | currencyrate.currencyratedate | currencyrate.fromcurrencycode | currencyrate.tocurrencycode | currencyrate.averagerate | currencyrate.endofdayrate | currencyrate.modifieddate
params.metric: pair_rate_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY currencyrate.fromcurrencycode, currencyrate.tocurrencycode ORDER BY currencyrate.currencyratedate DESC, currencyrate.currencyrateid DESC) | Note: averagerate and endofdayrate are passthrough numeric columns (not aggregated) — they are measures at the currencyrate row grain.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like tables or views keyed 1:1 to the currency pair (fromcurrencycode, tocurrencycode) — safe because this view is at most one row per currencyrateid and ranked so selecting pair_rate_rank = 1 yields one row per (fromcurrencycode,tocurrencycode). Example: join to a currency metadata table on currencycode = fromcurrencycode or currencycode = tocurrencycode if that table is 1:1 per currency code. | safe: join to currency metadata/dimension on currencycode = fromcurrencycode (or tocurrencycode) — no duplication of this view's measures when the metadata is one-row-per-currency. | safe: join to any view that is 1:1 with currencyrateid (if such exists) using currencyrateid. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views keyed only by fromcurrencycode or tocurrencycode that contain multiple rows per currency (for example, a table of historical annotations, many category assignments, or aggregated daily trends without reducing to one row per pair) — doing so will duplicate rows from this view and thus multiply its measures (averagerate/endofdayrate) unless you re-aggregate after the join. | do NOT join directly to sibling AGG or RANK views that are many-per-(fromcurrencycode,tocurrencycode) (for example, time-series trend tables that contain multiple dates per pair) unless you first filter this view to pair_rate_rank = 1 and then ensure the join key produces a one-to-one or many-to-one mapping. If joining to a many-per-pair source is required, either aggregate that source to one row per pair first or re-aggregate the combined result to avoid measure duplication. | when composing metrics that convert amounts using these rates, prefer selecting only rows with pair_rate_rank = 1 (latest) and then performing currency conversion joins on (fromcurrencycode,tocurrencycode) to ensure a single applicable rate per pair. | explicit example (safe): SELECT ... FROM currencyrate_latest_per_pair v JOIN currency_dim d ON d.currencycode = v.fromcurrencycode WHERE v.pair_rate_rank = 1; | explicit example (unsafe without re-aggregation): joining v (filtered to pair_rate_rank = 1) to sales_orders_flat which contains many orders per currency without aggregating sales_orders_flat — this will multiply v's rows if the join key is not uniquely 1:1; instead aggregate sales_orders_flat to one row per (fromcurrencycode,tocurrencycode) or join from orders to the latest rate in a many-to-one direction (orders -> latest rate) so each order picks one rate row.

views.description: Latest currency rate per (fromcurrencycode, tocurrencycode) pair using currencyratedate. One row per currency pair holding the most recent rates and dates. | Use for: Get latest exchange rate per currency pair for conversions; Trend analysis of exchange rates by pair
